lan.title: Direct Upload (LAN)
lan.desc: Install the “Samsung Health Viz Uploader” app on your phone, point it at the export folder from Samsung Health “Download personal data”, and the app packs it into a ZIP and uploads it to this computer — same Wi-Fi, no cable, no manual copying. The desktop app parses it automatically on arrival and refreshes the data.
lan.firewallHint: If the system asks about firewall permission the first time, allow “Samsung Health Viz” to access the local network.
lan.address: Computer address (enter this in the phone app)
lan.altUrls: If the first address fails, try:
lan.step1: Put the phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi; the phone app discovers this computer automatically, or enter the address above manually.
lan.step2: In the app, enter the token, pick the Samsung Health export folder and tap “Start upload”.
lan.step3: Keep this page open to watch progress; parsing and cache refresh happen automatically when done.

stadia.title: Basemap (Stadia Maps)
stadia.desc: The 9 Stadia Maps basemaps (Alidade / Outdoors / Stamen / OSM Bright) need an API key to load tiles; the desktop app cannot use localhost keyless access. Create a free account, generate a key in the console and paste it below; the key is stored on this machine only and never enters the repo or the installer.
stadia.hint: The free plan excludes “Alidade Satellite” (requires Stadia Standard or above). If tiles.stadiamaps.com needs a proxy, make sure the system proxy is on (Electron follows the system proxy).
stadia.dialogTitle: Stadia basemaps need an API key
stadia.dialogDesc: Stadia Maps basemaps (Alidade / Outdoors / Stamen / OSM Bright) need an API key to load tiles on desktop. Create a free account, generate a key in the console and paste it below.
stadia.dialogHint: The key is stored on this machine only.

parsed.title: What gets parsed
parsed.item1: com.samsung.shealth.exercise.csv: filters exercise type 11007 (cycling) and reads start/end time, duration, distance, calories, elevation gain, avg/max heart rate and other summary fields.
parsed.item2: jsons/com.samsung.shealth.exercise/*/UUID.location_data.json: per-second GPS points (lat/lon, altitude, time), downsampled and simplified with Douglas-Peucker into map tracks.
parsed.item3: jsons/.../UUID.live_data.json: in-workout samples for the speed curve and per-km splits; estimated from distance deltas when missing.
parsed.item4: com.samsung.shealth.tracker.heart_rate.csv + binning_data.json: when live_data has no heart rate, the minute-level HR buckets fill in the HR curve.
parsed.item5: exercise.weather / exercise.recovery_heart_rate: weather and recovery HR joined by exercise_id.

notes.title: Notes & limits
notes.item1: This app parses read-only; it never modifies the original package and all data stays on this machine.
notes.item2: Cycling detection is based on the Samsung internal code 11007; if your package uses a different code, the parser needs extending.
notes.item3: Map coordinates: the export has no explicit datum field, but phone-written track points carry version (GCJ-02) while watch tracks do not (WGS-84); parsing detects this and reprojects per basemap (AMAP GCJ-02 / OSM & satellite WGS-84) automatically.
notes.item4: This app only handles cycling; steps, sleep, heart rate and other data in the same package are out of scope.

welcome.title: Put your Samsung Health data on the map
welcome.sub: Import a data package exported from Samsung Health; rides and GPS tracks are parsed automatically into local maps and statistics.
welcome.lanHint: No cable? Turn on receiving on the “Settings” page, install the uploader app from the repo on your phone, pick the export folder and upload in one tap.
welcome.step1: In the Samsung Health phone app → Settings → Download personal data, get samsunghealth_<phone>_<time>.zip
welcome.step2: Pick the ZIP here (or extract first and choose the folder); rides and tracks are parsed
welcome.step3: When parsing finishes you land on the “Career” page; data is processed locally, and you can swap packages any time on the “Settings” page
welcome.privacy: 🔒 All parsing happens locally; the package is never uploaded. Parse results are cached in the app data directory.
